attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post.

semantics.note: An unhedged present-tense statement that the promised major productivity jumps have not appeared. The drafter's version is faithful.

contract.note: Reading this as aggregate, economy-wide gains is the ordinary reading. Picking Q4 2024 as the latest reportable quarter is reasonable. The contract says US evidence alone cannot settle a worldwide claim.

evidence.note: The Fed's Feb 2025 report says AI's effect on measured productivity was probably small. It is hedged, covers AI in general rather than GenAI, and is US-only.
Self-reported time savings from a Nov 2024 survey. The authors say it is uncertain whether this shows up in measured aggregate productivity, so it does not meet the contract's measure.
A 2023 Goldman forecast of gains over ten years. It shows a promise existed but sets no expectation for early 2025.

reviews.rationale: The Fed's hedged, US-only judgement that AI's effects were probably small points toward Marcus being right. But nothing in the packet isolates GenAI's contribution to aggregate productivity in the target quarter, the official BLS release could not be read, and the contract bars US evidence alone from establishing a worldwide conclusion. The survey time savings are self-reported, not measured output. The evidence does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own parenthetical in his own post.

semantics.note: The present-tense part ('most are losing money; few have made any profits') is correctly separated from the forecast about meagre profits.

contract.note: Counting companies, using 2024 as the period and treating 'any profits' as historical are ordinary readings. The company population is undefined, which makes the claim hard to test.

evidence.note: Anthropic's audited S-1 shows a $8.3B net loss for 2024 and losses in every year since founding. This fits Marcus's description for one company but cannot establish a majority.
Alphabet's consolidated net income does not separate out its model-building business. This is a company disclosure and not decisive either way.

reviews.rationale: Only two companies are covered: one loss-maker (Anthropic) and one diversified parent with consolidated profits (Alphabet). Neither a defined population nor any company count is available, so the evidence cannot show whether most were losing money or whether only a few had ever been profitable.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: 'The end game ... will be virtually free' is unhedged, so it is a forecast. It has no deadline.

contract.note: Reading the claim as negligible prices for ordinary use across the market is fair. The contract invents no deadline and does not treat positive prices today as a refutation.

evidence.note: GPT-5 was launched with a free tier, limited by usage. That shows LLMs are still available and partly free, but not a lasting market-wide end state.
Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite is cheap but still paid. A single model's price cannot settle the market-wide forecast.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. By the cutoff, neither of the contract's early-resolution events had happened: no lasting market-wide shift to negligible prices, and no disappearance of LLM services. Free tiers and falling prices are context only.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The revised wording restores 'enormously' and 'particularly'. It is a present-tense evaluative observation.

contract.note: Reading 'unreliable' as widely used assistants making material factual and sourcing errors is fair and ordinary, and the contract does not require every answer to be wrong. The Jan–Mar 2025 window is reasonable.

evidence.note: OpenAI's figure of 400M weekly users in Feb 2025, reported by TechCrunch. It is a company disclosure, but it plausibly shows enormous adoption.
Independent Feb 2025 tests of eight assistants found over 60% of answers incorrect, usually without any signal of uncertainty. Citing news sources is only one task.
OpenAI's own benchmark gains for GPT-4.5 show progress but do not establish that answers can be trusted in general.

reviews.rationale: Mass adoption is documented within the target period. Independent tests of eight prominent systems found frequent confident sourcing errors and little acknowledgement of uncertainty, which meets the contract's support condition. OpenAI's benchmark improvements do not show dependable factual accuracy, so they do not meet the contradiction condition.
